answers.rationale: Both quarantined and loaded v9 rows have totals exactly 100x the captured amount; the checkout team's statement (E06) is contradicted by the samples.
R1 catches only inflated totals above 50,000; inflated totals below it passed validation and were loaded between 02:05 and 02:40.
RSD rows match payment captures; they fail only because the reference list predates the market launch.
Night-time RSD-only windows were 1.8-2.4%, but daytime RSD share is unobserved with no forecast.
Windows containing only RSD quarantines stayed at 1.8-2.4%; the threshold was crossed only as R1 failures from v9 accumulated after 02:05.
v9 produces the inflated totals that R1 rejects.
The outdated list produces false-positive quarantines of valid RSD rows; the control's configuration, not the data, is the failure here.
Since 02:41 the breaker has stopped further inflated v9 rows that pass R1 from loading; containment is partial because rows loaded before the trip.
The halt is what makes the tables stale; the protective control produces this visible symptom without producing the underlying data failure.
The monitor reports staleness; it neither causes nor limits it.
Inflated totals below 50,000 pass R1; R1 neither detects nor contains them.
Loading is halted by the breaker, which persisted long after the vacuum ended at 02:55.
Loyalty events come from a separate code path whose v9 behaviour is unchecked, and accruals have not been examined.
v9 is still running, and its inflated totals below 50,000 pass validation; without the breaker they would load into the tables used for the close.
Removes the failure-producing mechanism.
Correctly tunes a control whose configuration is producing false positives, while leaving R2 active against genuinely invalid currencies (E15).
Would let the inflated totals R1 currently catches pass into the loader, hiding the corruption R1 is detecting.
Addresses the corruption that escaped containment before the breaker tripped.
The quarantined RSD rows are shown to be valid; releasing them after fixing the list restores correct data.
Targets a job with no relation to the halt.

hardness.reasoningChain: v9 canary writes 100x totals (E06, E07) -> large inflated totals fail R1 and are quarantined, small ones pass and load (E07, E08) -> R1 failures push the combined quarantine rate over 5% on top of RSD false positives (E03, E04, E05) -> breaker halts loading at 02:41 (E02) -> tables stale and freshness monitor alerts (E01). Disabling the breaker would resume loading of inflated sub-50,000 totals while v9 still runs.
constructTraps: Treating the breaker as the cause of the incident because it produces the visible staleness.
Accepting that validation caught all bad rows (E10) when R1 cannot see inflated totals below its bound.
Refusing to adjust R2 even though its reference data is demonstrably out of date.
